cards.title: Babies don't realize hidden toys still exist until around eight months old
cards.body: Place a blanket over a favorite toy in front of a six-month-old infant, and they will not search for it. Developmental psychologist Jean Piaget identified this as a lack of object permanence: to the infant's developing brain, objects out of sight literally cease to exist. Only between eight and twelve months do infants begin to understand that physical objects continue to exist even when hidden from view.

cards.title: Your brain literally turns 3D objects in your mind at a steady speed
cards.body: When psychologists Roger Shepard and Jacqueline Metzler showed participants pairs of complex 3D shapes rotated at various angles, they observed something remarkable. The time it took people to determine whether the shapes were identical was directly proportional to the rotation angle. Instead of calculating abstract geometry, the human visual cortex physically rotates a mental model through imaginary space, turning the object at a steady rate of about 60 degrees per second.

cards.title: Switching your door doubles your odds of winning—even if your brain rebels
cards.body: In the famous Monty Hall puzzle, you pick one of three doors hiding a car behind one and goats behind two. After the host reveals a goat behind another door, your intuition insists the two remaining doors offer equal 50/50 odds. But switching doors actually doubles your winning probability from one-third to two-thirds. The puzzle exposed how poorly human intuition handles conditional probability, famously baffling thousands of mathematicians.

cards.title: OCD isn't a passion for neatness—it is an exhausting cycle of terror
cards.body: Popular culture frequently treats obsessive-compulsive disorder as a harmless quirk about organized desk drawers or clean surfaces. In clinical reality, OCD is a severe anxiety condition driven by intrusive, terrifying thoughts, known as obsessions, such as fears of harming loved ones or catastrophic contamination. Patients perform repetitive, ritualized compulsions not out of tidiness, but as desperate, temporary attempts to neutralize overwhelming distress.

cards.title: ADHD isn't a lack of attention—it is a disorder of attention regulation
cards.body: People often assume attention deficit hyperactivity disorder simply makes someone incapable of focusing. In reality, ADHD is a neurodevelopmental disorder affecting executive function and dopamine signaling. While initiating focus on unstimulating tasks is intensely difficult, individuals with ADHD frequently experience "hyperfocus"—a state of deep, hours-long immersion in captivating activities, often to the point of forgetting to eat or sleep. The core issue is regulating attention, not lacking it.

quizzes.question: What does an infant under eight months old typically do when a toy is covered with a blanket?
options: Search underneath the blanket
Lose interest because they believe it ceased to exist
Cry and point at the blanket
Wait patiently for it to reappear
quizzes.explanation: Young infants lack object permanence, meaning they do not understand that objects continue to exist when hidden.

quizzes.question: How does the brain determine if two 3D shapes rotated at different angles match?
options: By applying instant trigonometric formulas
By scanning only the exterior silhouette
By mentally rotating the 3D shape through space at a steady speed
By converting the shapes into verbal descriptions
quizzes.explanation: Shepard and Metzler showed reaction times increase linearly with angle, showing the brain rotates a mental model through space.

quizzes.question: In the Monty Hall problem, what happens to your odds of winning the car if you switch doors?
options: They stay at 50%
They double from 1/3 to 2/3
They decrease from 1/2 to 1/3
They triple from 1/4 to 3/4
quizzes.explanation: Your initial choice had a 1/3 chance of winning, leaving a 2/3 chance with the other doors; switching captures that 2/3 probability.

quizzes.question: In clinical psychology, what is the primary purpose of compulsions in OCD?
options: To achieve perfect aesthetic order
To temporarily neutralize distress caused by obsessive thoughts
To practice disciplined habits
To seek attention from family members
quizzes.explanation: Compulsions in OCD are repetitive behaviors performed to alleviate the overwhelming anxiety triggered by intrusive, distressing obsessions.

quizzes.question: How does ADHD affect attention, according to modern clinical psychology?
options: It completely prevents a person from concentrating on anything
It is a disorder of attention regulation, not a total absence of focus
It only affects physical hyperactivity in childhood
It makes people permanently immune to boredom
quizzes.explanation: ADHD affects executive function and dopamine regulation, making it hard to direct focus voluntarily despite often allowing intense hyperfocus.

guesses.prompt: At roughly what speed, in degrees per second, does the human mind rotate a mental 3D image to solve a visual puzzle?
guesses.explanation: Psychologists found that mental rotation occurs at a remarkably steady rate of approximately 60 degrees per second.

guesses.prompt: In the Monty Hall problem, what percentage chance do you have of winning the car if you switch doors?
guesses.explanation: Switching doors captures the initial 2/3 (approximately 67%) probability that the car was behind one of the two unpicked doors.

misconceptions.claim: Infants under six months old understand that a toy still exists when it is hidden under a blanket.
misconceptions.explanation: Before developing object permanence around 8 months, infants treat out-of-sight objects as if they ceased to exist.

misconceptions.claim: When one losing door is revealed in the Monty Hall problem, switching gives you a 50% chance of winning.
misconceptions.explanation: Switching gives you a 2/3 (roughly 67%) chance of winning, because your initial door only had a 1/3 chance of being correct.

misconceptions.claim: Obsessive-compulsive disorder is primarily an intense personality preference for tidiness and symmetry.
misconceptions.explanation: Clinical OCD is an anxiety disorder driven by terrifying, intrusive thoughts and exhausting compulsions performed to relieve panic.

misconceptions.claim: People diagnosed with ADHD can sometimes focus on a captivating activity for hours without interruption.
misconceptions.explanation: ADHD is an executive dysfunction of attention regulation; individuals often experience intense 'hyperfocus' on highly stimulating tasks.
